questions.question: Before driving, check that air reaches all trailers by:

options.text: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for air escape.
Closing the rear shut-off valves and listening for air escape.
Disconnecting air supply lines and listening for air escape.
Rolling each trailer down a hill and testing the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for air escape.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, make sure air pressure reaches all trailers. Wait for air pressure to build. Then send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, air is being supplied to the whole vehicle.

questions.question: If a load is placed on one side of a trailer, the trailer:

options.text: May lean during turns.
May add extra support during turns.
May be easier to steer during turns.

questions.explanation: A load placed on one side of a trailer can cause it to lean to that side. This increases the risk of a rollover during turns and lane changes.

questions.question: When coupling:

options.text: You can assume all vehicles are the same.
Make sure you couple correctly.
Cracks in the mounting are acceptable.

questions.explanation: Incorrect coupling and uncoupling of combination vehicles can be extremely dangerous.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to skid, the driver should:

options.text: Lock the brakes.
Release the brakes.
Steer in the opposite direction.
Accelerate.

questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes. Let the wheels regain traction. Once traction returns, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: Not keeping the fifth wheel plate properly greased could:

options.text: Cause the trailer to disconnect.
Cause steering problems.
Cause braking problems.
Affect the lights.

questions.explanation: A dry fifth wheel plate creates friction between the tractor and trailer. This friction causes steering problems.

questions.question: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, you should prevent it from moving by:

options.text: Parking it against a wall or another vehicle.
Using wheel chocks.
Parking on a slight incline.

questions.explanation: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, use wheel chocks to prevent it from moving.

questions.question: If you are unsure if a trailer has ABS, you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
Try driving on a slippery surface to see if ABS activates.
Assume it has ABS.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). A yellow warning light shows if ABS is present. For older trailers, check under them for sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes.

questions.question: If an air supply control is in the "emergency" position:

options.text: The vehicle will increase speed.
The trailer emergency brakes will apply.
The air supply to the trailer will increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes will apply.
questions.explanation: Older vehicles may have lever controls instead of knobs. If an air supply control is set to "emergency", the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes apply.

questions.question: If you push the tractor air supply control and the trailer's spring brakes do not release, you should:

options.text: Check the air line connections.
Activate the Anti-Lock Braking System.
Turn the engine off and on again.

questions.explanation: All equipment must work properly before starting a trip. If spring brakes do not release when you push the tractor air supply control, make sure the air line connections are properly attached and sealed.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve will pop out when:

options.text: Air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
The trailer jackknifes.
Wheels regain traction after a skid.
Air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out if air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the protection valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: A combination vehicle has ____ air line(s).

options.text: One
Two
Three

questions.explanation: A combination vehicle has two air lines: one for service and one for emergencies.

questions.question: When driving while pulling trailers, you should:

options.text: Make sudden turns with the steering wheel.
Avoid making sudden moves.
Push the accelerator to the floor when starting from a stop.

questions.explanation: Steer gently and smoothly when pulling a trailer. Sudden steering movements can cause the trailer to tip over.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle goes around a corner:

options.text: The turn should be made as tightly as possible.
The front and rear wheels move in different paths.
The rear wheels should run over the curb.
It is acceptable for street signs to be knocked over if they are too close to the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels move in different paths.
questions.explanation: The rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels when turning. This is especially true for vehicles with trailers.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, you should not:

options.text: Release the brakes.
Apply the trailer hand brake.
Allow the wheels to grip the road.
Allow the trailer to straighten out.

questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes and let the wheels grip the road again. Do not apply the trailer hand brake, as it will make the skid worse. Brakes caused the problem in the first place.

questions.question: The ____ trailer is most likely to turn over if a driver takes a turn too quickly.

options.text: Front
Last
Middle

questions.explanation: The last trailer is most likely to roll over if you turn too quickly. Always steer gently and smoothly when pulling trailers.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: To accelerate in rural areas.
Only to test the trailer brakes.
Together with the brake pedal.
On slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: Use the trailer hand valve only to test the trailer brakes. Using it while the vehicle is moving can cause a skid.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
A valve that prevents the truck from being stolen
A valve that prevents the driver from going too fast
A valve that prevents the trailer from accidentally being released

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer:

options.text: Make sure to couple matching glad hands.
Any glad hand can be connected to any other glad hand.
It is best to leave one glad hand unattached.
Only one set of glad hands should be connected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure to couple matching glad hands.
questions.explanation: Connect matching glad hands when coupling. They are often color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is typically for service lines and red is for emergency lines.

questions.question: Before beginning a trip, you should:

options.text: Leave the service line valve open.
Remove the relay valves.
Close the emergency line valve.

questions.explanation: Before a trip, open the rear emergency and service line shut-off valves to check for air. Then close both shut-off valves before driving.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve will pop out when air pressure drops to:

options.text: 20 and 45 psi
75 and 105 psi
50 and 65 psi

questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, it closes to stop the flow of air.
